name: Microscopium
introduction: is the Microscope, a small, faint constellation introduced by Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in the 1750s, south of Capricornus.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Microscopium contains [Lacaille 8760](id:10pc-0060), one of the brightest red dwarfs in the sky, about 13 light-years away and just below naked-eye visibility. Red dwarfs are the most common stars in the galaxy, yet not one is bright enough to see without a telescope.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Gamma Microscopii](hip:103738), [Epsilon Microscopii](hip:105140) and [Alpha Microscopii](hip:102831) are the brightest stars, all fainter than fourth magnitude.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The young red dwarf AU Microscopii, about 32 light-years away, is surrounded by an edge-on disk of dust in which Hubble spotted fast-moving ripples, and it has at least two planets.
